etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English epiphanie, from Old French epyphanie, from Late Latin epiphania, from Ancient Greek ἐπιφάνεια (epipháneia, “manifestation, striking appearance”), from ἐπιφαίνω (epiphaínō, “I appear, display”), from ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “I shine, appear”). English Epiphany (of Christ) since the 14th century, generic use since the 17th century.
senses: (countable) An illuminating realization or discovery, often resulting in a personal feeling of elation, awe, or wonder.
(countable) A manifestation or appearance of a divine or superhuman being.
